answer.rationale: Constraints dominate: 14 days to expiry, line at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, and only one decision available. Any action that introduces new-supplier ramp risk right now (switch_primary_vendor) is the wrong shape of bet — memory_c2 records that the low-cost vendor cut unit cost sharply but missed the delivery SLA in three of four quarters and explicitly warns against sole-sourcing a critical line. That is precisely the trap the 18% spend mandate creates: cost pressure makes the cheapest quote look like the answer while the delivery-risk half of the objective silently absorbs the damage. Defer_decision is also unsafe here because the contract does not auto-renew — deferral is not a neutral hold (unlike memory_c5, where the service continued month-to-month), it is an uncovered gap on a line with no buffer. Add_second_source (memory_c3) is the right long-run structural move and should be the next cycle's decision, but it adds resilience rather than the in-year savings finance mandated, and qualifying a second source takes longer than 14 days. That leaves negotiate_terms: memory_c4 shows benchmarking against market rates moved the incumbent on both price and payment terms, and memory_c1 shows the incumbent relationship carries zero migration cost and no delivery interruption. Competing quotes from the low-cost vendor become negotiating leverage rather than a delivery commitment. I want the two verifications where the source record could actually flip the plan: memory_c2, because the magnitude and recency of the SLA misses determine whether that vendor is even credible leverage or a real second-source candidate next cycle; and memory_c4, because if that renegotiation win was small, one-off, or driven by conditions that no longer hold, an 18% cut is not reachable through price alone and I would need to reopen scope, volume, or specification with finance rather than promise a number I cannot hit. One caution on memory_c6: multi-year commitment unlocked volume pricing, but locking a long term now would forfeit the optionality to add a second source later, so I will target a shorter term with benchmarked pricing and hold dual-sourcing open. I do not yet know that negotiation alone closes the full 18%; that gap stays explicit rather than assumed away.
